"""Tiny inventory tracker for small restaurants.
Tracks on-hand counts, uses sales to estimate usage, flags low stock,
and drafts a supplier order from recent usage."""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass
class Item:
    name: str
    on_hand: float
    unit_cost: float
    par: float          # target stock level
    usage_per_week: float = 0.0

@dataclass
class Inventory:
    items: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def add(self, item: Item):
        self.items[item.name] = item

    def record_usage(self, name: str, used: float):
        self.items[name].on_hand -= used

    def low_stock(self, threshold=0.25):
        return [i.name for i in self.items.values()
                if i.on_hand <= i.par * threshold]

    def draft_order(self):
        order = {}
        for i in self.items.values():
            target = max(i.par, i.usage_per_week * 2)
            need = target - i.on_hand
            if need > 0:
                order[i.name] = round(need, 1)
        return order

if __name__ == "__main__":
    inv = Inventory()
    inv.add(Item("chicken thighs (lb)", on_hand=12, unit_cost=2.8, par=40, usage_per_week=30))
    inv.add(Item("rice (lb)", on_hand=60, unit_cost=0.9, par=50, usage_per_week=25))
    inv.add(Item("limes (ct)", on_hand=6, unit_cost=0.3, par=30, usage_per_week=20))
    inv.record_usage("limes (ct)", 4)
    print("Low stock:", inv.low_stock())
    print("Draft order:", inv.draft_order())

# Units: parents' sheet logs cases as "2 cs (24 ct)" and weights as "4.5 lb".
# Normalize everything to a base unit per item so counts from both formats compare.
import re

def parse_qty(text: str, units_per_case: float = 1.0) -> float:
    """'2 cs (24 ct)' -> 48 ct (explicit per-case count in parentheses);
    '2 cs' -> 2 * units_per_case; '4.5 lb' -> 4.5. Returns base unit (each / lb)."""
    text = text.strip().lower()
    if text.endswith("lb"):
        return float(text[:-2].strip())
    m = re.match(r"^([\d.]+)\s*cs\b(?:\s*\(([\d.]+)\s*ct\))?", text)
    if m:
        cases = float(m.group(1))
        per_case = float(m.group(2)) if m.group(2) else units_per_case
        return cases * per_case
    return float(text.split()[0])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert parse_qty("2 cs (24 ct)") == 48
    assert parse_qty("4.5 lb") == 4.5
    assert parse_qty("3 cs", units_per_case=12) == 36
    assert parse_qty("7 ct") == 7
    print("parse_qty OK:", parse_qty("2 cs (24 ct)"))
